documents.unit: Rutgers Office of Information Technology (all campuses)
documents.title: Guidance on the use of AI at Rutgers
documents.summary: Short OIT guidance shared by all Rutgers campuses. It says academic AI rules vary by discipline, course and instructor, and that AI is not permissible for coursework unless instructors say so. It also covers approved tools, confidential data, verifying output and purchasing.
documents.stance_why: The page says academic AI guidance "will typically vary depending on the discipline, course, and/or instructor" and AI is not permissible "unless clearly stated or communicated by instructors", so the decision is handed to instructors, which is delegates.

units.why: The sentence says "only Rutgers-approved AI tools should be used at the university", a directive to use vetted tools to protect data; it is a data-protection and vetted-tool rule (P50) and applies to everyone.
units.anchor: only Rutgers-approved AI tools should be used at the university

units.why: "The tools licensed by Rutgers include security and privacy safeguards" describes the sanctioned licensed tools OIT provides; this fits a sanctioned university tool (P17).
units.anchor: provides access to generative AI tools with protections for use in university work
units.fit_note: Also says approved versions come with security and privacy safeguards.

units.why: "will not be used to train the models" is a stated privacy protection of approved tools, so it explains why vetted tools are preferred (P50, protect data and prefer vetted tools).
units.anchor: your data will not be used to train the models underlying the tools

units.why: "will typically vary depending on the discipline, course, and/or instructor" leaves the academic-use decision to instructors, so P04, not a university-set rule.
units.anchor: guidance on the appropriate use of AI tools in academic settings will typically vary
units.frag_start: At Rutgers, guidance on the appropriate

units.why: "Faculty should consider providing guidance to students" asks instructors to communicate AI expectations, though softly ("consider"); nearest type is P09 (state expectations), hence a fit note.
units.anchor: Faculty should consider providing guidance to students on the use of AI
units.fit_note: Only "should consider" providing guidance, not a mandatory syllabus statement.

units.why: "students are encouraged to review course materials and speak with their instructors" tells students to check expectations with instructors, matching P10 (ask before using AI).
units.anchor: students are encouraged to review course materials and speak with their instructors
units.frag_end: any specific expectations related to AI

units.why: "should not be considered permissible for coursework unless clearly stated or communicated by instructors" sets the default when instructors are silent: not allowed. That is the fallback rule (P06); it is "should not", softer than a ban.
units.anchor: they should not be considered permissible for coursework unless clearly stated or communicated by instructors
units.frag_start: Though AI tools are widely available

units.why: "Students are responsible for understanding and abiding by their program and instructors' guidance" puts the duty to know and follow AI rules on students; nearest is P29 (responsibility), with a fit note.
units.anchor: Students are responsible for understanding and abiding by their program and instructors’ guidance
units.frag_end: rules on the use of AI
units.fit_note: Responsibility is for knowing and following AI rules, not ownership of submitted work.

units.why: The quotation that coursework be "created without the aid of impermissible technologies" ties unauthorized AI use to the Academic Integrity Policy, i.e. treating it as an integrity matter (P36).
units.anchor: the student’s own and created without the aid of impermissible technologies, materials, or collaborations
units.frag_start: the principles of academic integrity require

units.why: "Confidential information, Protected Health Information (PHI), and other proprietary Rutgers information may not be appropriate for use in AI applications" warns against entering sensitive data, which is data protection (P50).
units.anchor: Protected Health Information (PHI), and other proprietary Rutgers information may not be appropriate for use
units.fit_note: Hedged ("may not be appropriate") and about confidential and proprietary university information.

units.why: "Always review and verify AI content and outputs" is a direct instruction to check AI output, P31.
units.anchor: Always review and verify AI content and outputs

units.why: "AI tools can produce biased and inaccurate information, and may include copyrighted information without attribution" names bias and copyright risks; bias/harm fits P53 best, and P52 is not chosen since no ownership rule is stated.
units.anchor: AI tools can produce biased and inaccurate information, and may include copyrighted information without attribution
units.fit_note: Also notes copyrighted content without attribution and inaccuracy, which this type does not centre.

units.why: "You are responsible for ensuring the accuracy and appropriateness of AI-generated content used for university work" makes users own what they use, P29.
units.anchor: you must follow the same security processes and risk assessments

units.why: "you must follow the same security processes and risk assessments as for other software purchases" governs procurement of AI technology, an operational rule (P76); P65 vendor review is close but this is a purchase procedure, not contract or data-sharing limits.
units.frag_start: If you are considering the purchase of an AI
units.fit_note: Also requires digital accessibility standards; closest alternative P65.

units.why: The list says Academic Integrity, Information Classification and Acceptable Use policies "are particularly relevant for the use of AI at Rutgers", so AI use is bound by existing policies (P77).
units.anchor: are particularly relevant for the use of AI at Rutgers

notes: Single universitywide OIT page; no Camden-specific, school or computing documents. Course layer deferred.
